This Rp Is Filed Under Order 47 Rule 1 R/W Sec.
114 Of Cpc, Praying To Review The Order Dated
03.10.2016 In Mfa No.200332/2016 (Lac) By Modifying The
Judgment And Award Dated 19.04.2011 Passed By The
Learned Senior Civil Judge, Aland In Lac No.38/2009 On
Par With Annexure-A And Award Compensation.
 These Petitions Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

RP No.200040/2022 is filed to review the judgment dated 08.11.2016 passed by this Court in MFA No.200331/2016 and RP No.200046/2016 is filed to review the judgment dated 03.10.2015 passed by this Court in MFA No.200332/2016.
2.

The petitioners in these review petitions were the owners of the land bearing Survey Nos.151/1 and 152/1 measuring 2 acres 5 guntas and 2 acres 1 gunta respectively situated at Ambalaga village,
Kalaburagi NC: 2023:KHC-K:5594 taluka and district which was proposed for acquisition for the purpose of Gandori Nala Project in terms of a notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 15.09.2005.
An award was passed on 03.05.2008 determining the compensation payable at a sum of Rs.69,750/- per acre.

The petitioners not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded filed LAC Nos.37/2009 and 38/2009 respectively under Section 18(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short 'L.A. Act, 1894').
The Reference Court in terms of its judgment and award dated 19.04.2011 enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.2,42,000/- per acre.
Following this, the petitioners herein filed belated appeals before this Court in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016.
This Court in terms of the judgment dated 08.11.2016 and 03.10.2016 respectively dismissed the appeals as they were belated.
Feeling aggrieved by dismissal of the appeals, the petitioners filed SLP (Civil) Diary No.29331/2017.
The Apex Court in terms of its order NC: 2023:KHC-K:5594 dated 08.01.2018 dismissed SLP (Civil) Diary No.29331/2017 and granted the following liberty:

"However, we make it clear that in case the enhancement is granted in the pending appeal against the common award before the High Court, the petitioner will also be at liberty to move the High Court at that stage and his case may be considered on merits."

sentences.text: It is now stated that the appeals filed against the judgment and award passed by the reference Court concerning the same acquisition in MFA No.201595/2016 and connected appeals, this Court had enhanced the compensation to a sum of Rs.4,15,000/- per acre.
In view of the above, the petitioners have filed these review petitions to review the judgments dated 08.11.2016 and 03.10.2016 respectively passed in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that though the petitioners' appeals were dismissed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court, yet, in view of the judgment passed in the appeals arising out of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:5594 references in respect of the same acquisition, the petitioners are entitled to be treated alike in view of Section 28(A) of L.A. Act, 1894.
5.

Learned counsel for the respondents on the other hand submitted that the award passed by the Reference Court in LAC No.37/2009 was on 19.04.2011 and that there was a delay of 1675 days in filing the appeal before this Court in MFA No.200331/2016.
Similarly, in LAC No.38/2009, the judgment and award was passed by the Reference Court on 19.04.2011 while the appeal before this Court was filed belatedly in MFA No.200332/2016 after 1675 days.
He further submits that the Hon'ble Supreme Court disposed off the Special Leave Petition in the year 2016 and the petitioners have waited till the year 2022 to file the present review petitions.
He therefore contended that the petitioners are not entitled for interest for the period of delay.
Heard the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners as well as the learned counsel for the respondents.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioners did not dispute that the appeals filed before this Court in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016 were belated by 1675 days.

She also did not dispute the fact that even after disposal of Special Leave Petition before the Apex Court during the year 2016, no steps were taken to seek review of the judgment passed in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016 till the year 2022.
It is relevant to note that this Court disposed off several appeals arising out of acquisition for the same project under the same notification on 22.07.2021.

The delay if any in filing the review petitions from the date of the judgment of the Apex Court is properly explained and therefore, the petitioners are entitled to interest from the date of disposal of appeals before this Court in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016.
In that view of the matter, the impugned judgments passed by this Court in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016 are reviewed and recalled.

The appeals in MFA No.200331/2016 and MFA No.200332/2016 are allowed and the compensation of Rs.2,42,000/-
per acre awarded by the Reference Court in LAC Nos.37/2009 and 38/2009 is enhanced to a sum of Rs.4,15,000/- per acre.
However, the petitioners are entitled to interest and other benefits from 08.11.2016 and 03.10.2016 respectively.
The petitioners are also entitled to proportionate costs.
